title: DIC Versus TTP and HUS: Microangiopathic Patterns
subject: Pathology
preview: DIC causes systemic coagulation activation with consumption of platelets and factors, often prolonging coagulation tests.
quickRevision: DIC causes systemic coagulation activation with consumption of platelets and factors, often prolonging coagulation tests.
HUS includes microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and kidney injury, with different etiologies.
Smear schistocytes, kidney function, neurologic findings and coagulation profile help differentiate the syndromes.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: DIC causes systemic coagulation activation with consumption of platelets and factors, often prolonging coagulation tests.
TTP involves severe ADAMTS13 dysfunction and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with thrombocytopenia; coagulation tests are often not markedly prolonged.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: HUS includes microangiopathic hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and kidney injury, with different etiologies.
Smear schistocytes, kidney function, neurologic findings and coagulation profile help differentiate the syndromes.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not delay specialist evaluation for suspected TTP while waiting for every confirmatory result.
